raw.body:
React version: vendored in Next.js 16.2.6–16.2.9 and 16.3.0-canary.47. The same code is in `packages/react-dom-bindings/src/server/fizz-instruction-set/ReactDOMFizzInstructionSetShared.js` on `main` today.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Server-render a page with a Suspense boundary whose content streams in after the shell (any Next.js App Router page with a suspended segment works).
2. Open it in a background/hidden tab (or rely on Edge sleeping-tabs / Chromium window-occlusion on Windows) and keep it hidden until streaming finishes.
3. **Scenario A (never revealed):** `window.$RB` still holds the queued pair, the boundary marker is still `<!--$~-->`, fallback still in the DOM — nothing is interactive.
4. **Scenario B (revealed, never hydrated):** open the tab while the shell paints so `$RT` is set, then immediately hide it; streaming finishes, content moves into place via the `setTimeout` throttle path, but `_reactRetry` is never called — the page looks complete but all buttons are dead.

Manually running `marker.data = '$'; marker._reactRetry()` (or `window.$RV(window.$RB)` followed by invoking retries) un-wedges the page, which confirms the diagnosis.

No JS errors are thrown in either scenario.

## The current behavior

Both the batched boundary reveal (`$RV`) and the hydration retry are gated on `requestAnimationFrame`, which browsers never fire in hidden/occluded tabs:

1. The bootstrap sets `$RT` via `requestAnimationFrame(function(){$RT=performance.now()})`. In a hidden tab this rAF never fires, so `$RT` remains `undefined`.
2. `completeBoundary` (`$RC`) marks the boundary `<!--$~-->` (`SUSPENSE_QUEUED_START_DATA`), pushes it into `$RB`, and — because `typeof $RT !== 'number'` — schedules the flush with `requestAnimationFrame($RV.bind(null, $RB))`. That rAF never fires while hidden, so the boundary stays queued forever.
3. On the client, `registerSuspenseInstanceRetry` sees `$~` and parks the retry on `instance._reactRetry`; that callback is only invoked from inside `$RV`, which never ran.
4. Even in scenario B (tab visible at first paint so `$RT` is set, then hidden), `revealCompletedBoundaries` still re-defers `_reactRetry` via `requestAnimationFrame(suspenseNode._reactRetry)` — content is moved into place and painted, but hydration never runs.

Scenario B is the nastier production case: Chromium's window-occlusion detection on Windows can report `visibilityState === "hidden"` for a window the user is actively clicking, so they see a fully-painted page that never becomes interactive. We traced a real-world dead-click cluster (12 dead clicks on one button, Edge/Windows, zero JS errors) to exactly this.

## The expected behavior

Boundaries should reveal and hydrate even when the document is hidden. The rAF throttle is a paint heuristic; when there is no paint, there is nothing to throttle. Suggested fix: use `setTimeout(..., 0)` instead of `requestAnimationFrame` when `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'`, and/or flush any pending `$RB` entries and `_reactRetry` callbacks on `visibilitychange`.

**Workaround (in use):** we ship an inline script that, while `document.hidden`, periodically calls `window.$RV(window.$RB)` then walks comment nodes and invokes any `_reactRetry` still on `<!--$-->` markers (idempotent). Happy to share the full snippet.
raw.title: Bug: Streamed Suspense boundaries never reveal/hydrate in hidden or occluded tabs ($RV reveal and hydration retry are gated on requestAnimationFrame)
